input.question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?
input.ground_truth: Because you remember the best, eventful memories in more detail. You tend to block out all the normal things like changing you socks or taking a shit that day. Similar to when you zone out in the shower trying to think if you've just washed your hair or not. You do those things everyday and block them out of memory.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it when we look back at things in our past they seem a lot better than they actually are?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy that you really, really liked when you were a baby. Now, when you look at a picture of you playing with that toy, you remember how happy you were. But if you actually played with that toy now, it might be broken or not as fun as you remember.

When we think about things from the past, like fun times or cool toys, our brain likes to show us the happy parts and forget the not-so-good parts. It’s like only remembering the ice cream and not the time you dropped it on the floor! So, things from the past seem extra nice in our memories because our brain wants us to feel happy when we think about them.
